shorts.title: Secretary Birds Kick Snakes to Death 🦵
shorts.description:
This bird kicks snakes to death. A 2016 force-plate study clocked the kick at about 195 newtons with just 15 ms of contact.

#shorts #animalfacts #meatballmyths

Photos (iNaturalist), cropped and color-adjusted: Secretarybird: Jan Ebr & Ivana Ebrová (CC BY), CC0, avocat (CC BY), Luis G Restrepo (CC BY). creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0 · creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0
shorts.comment: Would you take a kick lesson from this bird? 👇

shorts.title: Archerfish Shoot Bugs Down With Water 💦
shorts.description:
Archerfish shoot bugs down with water. In a 2016 Scientific Reports study, trained archerfish picked a learned human face out of 44 new ones.

#shorts #animalfacts #meatballmyths

Photos (iNaturalist), cropped and color-adjusted: Archerfish: Pierre Pericard (CC BY), Andrew Parker (CC BY), Nicola Crockford (CC BY). creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0 · creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0
shorts.comment: Would you trust a fish that remembers your face? 👇

shorts.title: The One Thing a Gecko Can't Stick To 🦎
shorts.description:
Tokay geckos can climb almost anything. Gecko toes stick with van der Waals forces from millions of tiny spatulae; nonstick coatings and wet surfaces undermine the grip.

#shorts #animalfacts #meatballmyths

Photos (iNaturalist), cropped and color-adjusted: Tokay gecko: Kseniia Marianna Prondzynska (CC BY), Arky (CC BY), Sockrosma (CC BY). creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0 · creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0
shorts.comment: What did you guess the surface was? 👇

shorts.title: Glass Frogs Have See-Through Bellies 🐸
shorts.description:
Glass frogs have see-through bellies. Resting glassfrogs pack about 89% of their red blood cells into the liver and become 2-3 times more transparent (Taboada et al. 2022, Science).

#shorts #animalfacts #meatballmyths

Photos (iNaturalist), cropped and color-adjusted: Glass frog: Stephanie Tran (CC BY), Jared Shorma (CC BY), Fábio Olmos (CC BY), John G. Phillips (CC BY), Tom Kennedy (CC BY), CC0. creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0 · creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0
shorts.comment: Would you want a see-through belly? 👇

shorts.title: Armadillos Are Born as Identical Quadruplets 🐣
shorts.description:
Nine-banded armadillos have identical quadruplets. Despite the myth, nine-banded armadillos can't roll into a ball. Only three-banded armadillos can.

#shorts #animalfacts #meatballmyths

Photos (iNaturalist), cropped and color-adjusted: Nine-banded armadillo: CC0, Tristan Jobin (CC BY). creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0 · creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0
shorts.comment: Could you tell armadillo quadruplets apart? 👇

shorts.title: The Lyrebird's Strangest Fake Sound 🎶
shorts.description:
Lyrebirds steal other birds' songs. Male superb lyrebirds fake the alarm calls of a mobbing flock during courtship (Dalziell et al. 2021, Current Biology).

#shorts #animalfacts #meatballmyths

shorts.title: One Puffin Carried 62 Fish at Once 🐟
shorts.description:
One puffin held sixty-two fish at once. Puffins shed the bright outer plates of their beaks after the breeding season.

#shorts #animalfacts #meatballmyths

Photos (iNaturalist), cropped and color-adjusted: Atlantic puffin: Huey (CC BY), CC0, Frank Sengpiel (CC BY), ikelman (CC BY). creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0 · creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0
shorts.comment: How many fish could you carry in your mouth? 👇

shorts.title: How Wood Frogs Survive Freezing Solid 🧊
shorts.description:
Wood frogs freeze solid every winter. Glucose from the liver and urea act as antifreeze, protecting the frog's cells while it is frozen.

#shorts #animalfacts #meatballmyths

Photos (iNaturalist), cropped and color-adjusted: Wood frog: Stephanie Tran (CC BY), evangrimes (CC BY), Brian Gratwicke (CC BY), CC0. creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0 · creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0
shorts.comment: What was your guess before the reveal? 👇

shorts.title: Mudskippers Are Fish That Live on Land 🐟
shorts.description:
Mudskippers are fish that live on land. A 2023 PNAS study found mudskippers blink by retracting their eyes, mostly when they are on land.

#shorts #animalfacts #meatballmyths

Photos (iNaturalist), cropped and color-adjusted: Mudskipper: Ian Dugdale (CC BY), Bryce Watts-Parker (CC BY), Mohammad Amin Ghaffari (CC BY). creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0 · creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0
shorts.comment: Is a mudskipper more fish or more frog? 👇

shorts.title: The Pangolin's One Weakness 🛡️
shorts.description:
Pangolins are armored against lions. In 2023 scientists described a new pangolin lineage, Manis mysteria, from seized scales alone. No one has seen one alive.

#shorts #animalfacts #meatballmyths

shorts.title: The Ladybug's Gross Secret Weapon 🐞
shorts.description:
Ladybugs look totally harmless. This defense is called reflex bleeding: a foul-tasting alkaloid fluid released from the leg joints.

#shorts #animalfacts #meatballmyths
